title: Kaze
description: Lying in the long grass in July, looking up past the stalks into a deep summer sky, and the wind is yours. Brush across the frame and your stroke becomes a gust: it runs on through the grass, the tall brome and seed heads lean over under it across the clouds and swing back with a little overshoot, and the clouds behind drift faster after it. Left alone, a light breeze keeps them moving.
intent: Technique 10, Kaze (factory/reality/techniques.md): an Eulerian motion field you author live. A 96x64 stable-fluids velocity grid (Stam 1999, https://www.dgp.toronto.edu/public_user/stam/reality/Research/pdf/ns.pdf) carries the air in metres per second over the whole frame; each cell's grass is a damped spring driven by dynamic pressure. The grass is geometry seen worm's-eye: a 116 deg stereographic lens 4 cm off the ground, pitched so the zenith sits just above the top of the frame, and every blade, culm and brome panicle a world-space ribbon rooted below the bottom edge, so the stalks run up and converge on that vanishing point, the nearest long, the field behind a low fringe. Three culms with seed heads at your shoulder are the sharp near-black anchor (full resolution, 4x MSAA); the rest is drawn at half resolution, a touch diffused behind them. Edges are the blades' own MSAA coverage, premultiplied, with no matte or alpha test; the only warm in the grass is a thin halation ring on the blade edges that cross the sun. The wind bends each stalk about its root: the bend read at its tip on screen moves it level in the world by the bend times its lever (length times height along it squared), and it comes down a little as it lies over. The cumulus drift is a two-phase flow map (Vlachos 2010), faster toward the zenith, and leans after the gusts. ?gust=demo throws a scripted gust, ?t=seconds runs the wind that long and holds it, ?breeze=0..2 scales the idle air, ?debug=bend tints the grass by its bend.

sources.author: Forest Service, Northern Region (USDA), via Wikimedia Commons
sources.note: No longer drawn: the grass is now geometry (grass.js), and this photograph only fixes the frame the sky and the wind grid share (its uv; the sun is since moved to the frame's top left corner). Tall grass against partly cloudy skies, Tally Lake Ranger District, Flathead National Forest, Montana: camera at blade height pitched up. Display P3 converted to sRGB, worked at 2400x1600. Sky matte by tools/depth/segment.py sky (colour unmixing for thin blades), firmed by colour (sunlit brome is greener than the sky behind it) and darkness, and by a dark-object prior (a thin line clearly darker or greener than the sky inpainted behind it by a grey closing is all blade, so the brome crossing the sun stands solid); the sky behind thin grass is that closing, so the cloud texture runs on round the sun, which rolls off to warm white with its diffusion baked above a threshold; grass colour unmixed against a push-pull sky so a F + (1 - a) S recomposes the photograph. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/kaze/bake.py. Its own sky.webp is since replaced by the HDRI sky below.

sources.author: Greg Zaal (original), Jarod Guest (sky edits), Poly Haven
sources.note: The sky layer: a 3600x2400 pinhole view up into the HDRI, aimed so its sun lands in the frame's top left corner and rolled about it so the big cumulus runs off to the right along the top; printed with a soft local shoulder, the sun a warm white diffusion bloom with no disc, the cumulus lifted to warm white domes with pale skylight-blue shade, and the open sky a zenith gradient from pale cyan (hue ~200) low in the frame to deep cobalt at the top. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/kaze/sky_hdri.py.
